breaking.summary: Indian exporters are leaving much of the benefit of the country’s expanding free-trade network untapped, with only 20-30% of eligible shipments using preferential tariffs against 60-70% in partner countries, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said. As a result, 70-80% of eligible Indian exports continue to enter partner markets under regular most-favoured-nation (MFN) tariffs, making them less competitive than goods from countries that use trade agreements more effectively.

breaking.title: RBI Restores 90% Daily CRR Requirement From 1 Dec Amid Liquidity Tightening
breaking.summary: RBI reduces banks' daily CRR maintenance requirement from 99% to 90% from December 1, releasing Rs 50,000 crore amid tight liquidity. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to reduce the minimum daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance requirement for banks from 99 per cent to 90 per cent, effective 1 December 2026, as liquidity conditions in the banking system tighten and short-term interest rates rise. The move is expected to release around Rs 50,000 crore into the banking system, providing banks with additional liquidity at a time when the system has moved into a deficit.
